source_text: In traditional brit milah, anesthesia is not employed, as the procedure is performed swiftly by a trained mohel on the eighth day after birth, minimizing duration and relying on the infant's natural resilience, with a few drops of wine administered orally as a symbolic and mild analgesic. [55] [56]
